Deputy Prime Minister packet 36 (tonga-deputy-prime-ministers-1990-2026-36.md) adds 1990-2021 to_deputy_pm holder observations after the unchanged string observation to_cabinet_appointment and before the existing 2021-2025 holders: Langi Kavaliku (attested 2000-11-06), Tevita Poasi Tupou (2001-01-24 to 2001-09-28), James Cecil Cocker (attested 2002-05-13), Viliami Ta'u Tangi (attested 2006-08-08), Samiu Kuita Vaipulu (from 2011-01-04), Siaosi Sovaleni (attested 2014-12-31), Lord Ma'afu (from 2017-09-01), Semisi Kioa Lafu Sika (from 2018-01-05), Sione Vuna Fa'otusia (from 2019-10-09) and Lord Ma'afu (attested 2021-04-21, until his death on 2021-12-12). The Deputy Prime Minister of 1 January 1990 and most ends remain unresolved; acting service is recorded as claims only, and no complete term is claimed.
This is a bounded 1990-1991 source inventory: one party and three state institutions, not an exhaustive USSR party, faction, opposition, republic or coalition census.

The packet does not establish absence of other organizations. Discover original party registers, congresses, candidate organizations and opposition movements with separate union/republic jurisdiction.
Exact party election dates, acting roles, original spelling and full leadership intervals remain unresolved; contemporary Japanese diplomatic reporting is not an original CPSU election protocol.
1991 office changes, emergency claims, resignations, suspensions and dissolution require their own source review. No legal or organizational continuity through 2026 is inferred.
The USSR packet remains separate from Russia. Existing game party mappings, historical avatar eligibility, likeness approval and post-cutoff fictional succession are not changed.

CLAUDE-C01-05 reviews only the December 1991 records bearing on the Presidency (SURU-TR91-04 to 08). The August 1991 events, the CPSU suspension and the September 1991 changes to the Congress and Supreme Soviet remain unreviewed.

CLAUDE-C01-26 adds a fourth state institution, su_government (the Council of Ministers and, from 1991, the Cabinet of Ministers of the USSR), with one head-of-government role, and extends su_supreme_soviet_chair; it reviews the Union government's head and the Supreme Soviet's chair from 1 January 1990 to December 1991 (SU-GOV-01 to 10), including the August 1991 release decree, suspension and no-confidence vote and the September 1991 reorganisation of the Supreme Soviet. The CPSU's 1991 suspension and dissolution, the Congress's own end and the chamber chairmanships remain unreviewed, and no holder in either role has a from or an until.

CLAUDE-C01-35 adds two organizations: su_democratic_russia (the Democratic Russia movement, with the co-leadership role su_dr_co_chair) and su_soyuz_deputies_group (the Soyuz group of USSR people's deputies, with the co-leadership role su_soyuz_co_chair). It reviews their leaders from 1 January 1990 to 25 December 1991 (SU-DR-01 to 05, SU-SOYUZ-01 to 05) from Congress and Supreme Soviet stenograms and archival facsimiles of the movement's own papers and of the RSFSR President's office. Co-chairs are recorded as co-leadership, one person per observation; no holder has a from or an until. Neither organization is mapped to a simulation party row, and the RSFSR deputies' faction of the same name and the later organizations called «Союз» remain unreviewed.

CLAUDE-C01-41 dates the existing su_cpsu roles su_cpsu_general_secretary and su_cpsu_deputy_general_secretary from the party's own records (Pravda, the Central Committee's organ, and Известия ЦК КПСС, as Internet Archive stored files) and official Union records (the Supreme Soviet's and Congress's stenographic bulletins and Ведомости on the SSSR.SU host) and an RSFSR decree: three observations of Михаил Сергеевич Горбачев (5 February 1990, 10 July 1990, 22 August 1991) and two of Владимир Антонович Ивашко (13 July 1990, 21 August 1991), attested_on only, beside the unchanged S10.h month observations; 12 sources and 26 claims. The General Secretary's statement of 24 August 1991, the deputy's acting service and the party's dissolution remain unresolved; the suspension (29 August 1991) and the RSFSR decree (6 November 1991) are organization claims only.
